newsitem.title: USA: Argentina sees IMF approval of letter of intent.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees IMF approval of letter of intent.

text.p: Argentina is confident that the International Monetary Fund Board will approve its new letter of intent for a standby program later this month, Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Thursday.
"We are fully confident that this will be approved," Fernandez said at a news conference at the Argentine Embassy.
The letter of intent includes new economic targets for 1996 and 1997 for a $1.2 billion loan the IMF granted Argentina earlier this year.
Under the letter of intent Argentina will ask to be allowed to end 1996 with a $6 billion public sector deficit, rather than the $2.5 billion shortfall pledged in the original program.

Fernandez said that Argentina's proposal was bolstered by the recent approval by the Argentine Congress of tax increases he had submitted before travelling to Washington to the IMF-World Bank annual meeting.
According to Fernandez, the Argentine Congress's swift action was proof of strong political support for Argentina's economic program.
Fernandez also announced that Argentina will try to reschedule around $6 billion in undispersed loans from the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank.
"This is a big concern for Argentina because we are paying a commitment fee for the undispersed funds," he said.
Fernandez said that a committee will start working as soon as next week to try to work out a new schedule for the program supported by those loans.
Some of the projects, he said, were less of a priority for the Argentine government now than when the loans were originally granted.
Regarding the prospects for Argentina's economic recovery, Fernandez said he expected the Gross Domestic Product growth rate to reach at least five percent in 1997.
"We are in a frank recovery of the economic cycle," he said.
For 1996 the World Bank has forecast that Argentina's economy would grow around 2.5 percent, up from last year's 4.4 percent contraction.
